evidenceRule: Current profile/discipline/topics/methods where present; otherwise description2 considered fully within its actual supported scope. Evidence distinctions stay internal. No workbook alteration.
conceptsFrozenBeforeSelection: A programme combining energy resources, conversion and renewable-system design with mathematical modelling, probability, numerical methods and optimisation. Economics, law, qualitative research, EU policymaking, public-policy analysis and sustainability governance connect technological choices with public decisions and competing interests. Climate science and life-cycle assessment support evaluation of energy transitions. It provides a substantive interdisciplinary response to the Energy & Industry direction, with gaps in industrial-process engineering, agent-based and system-dynamics simulation, specialist infrastructure economics and safety, and Delft’s compulsory final project.

A programme centred on programming, software, databases and digital networks, supported by statistical learning, algorithms, probability, numerical methods and optimisation. Law, economics, public-policy analysis, AI ethics and organisational research address the institutional and social decisions surrounding digital systems. Its priority is computational analysis and the governance of digital change, rather than energy technology. Technical projects are not guaranteed to concern public policy; the programme does not reproduce Delft’s full engineering-and-policy sequence or its compulsory final project.

courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.contribution: Mandatory personal, academic and professional development, with writing and community engagement; not substituted for disciplinary research.

courses.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
courses.contribution: Direct: AI innovation, labour, business organisation, governance and regulation connect digital tools with institutional and economic consequences; no technical AI content is inferred.

courses.name: Introduction to Economics
courses.contribution: Direct: microeconomic choice, markets and macroeconomic policy foundations support analysis of incentives and market-government relations.

courses.name: Public Economics
courses.contribution: Direct: public goods, externalities, taxation and efficiency/equity supply policy-economics tools; not a substitute for dedicated infrastructure contracts and regulation.

courses.name: Research Methods & Statistics
courses.contribution: Direct: research design, sampling, experimentation and inferential statistics underpin empirical analysis of decisions and policy.

courses.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
courses.contribution: Complementary: organisational psychology across people, teams and structures, with a systematic review, supports the organisational side of digital change; not public law or technical systems engineering.

courses.name: AI Ethics
courses.contribution: Direct: AI ethics and social consequences examine responsibility, fairness and human values in digital decision systems; not the whole external safety course.

courses.name: Decision-making in AI
courses.contribution: Direct: probabilistic/Bayesian reasoning, Markov decision models, expected utility and multi-agent decisions analyse uncertainty and decision behaviour; no public-policy application is assumed.

courses.name: Optimization Methods in AI
courses.contribution: Direct: search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimisation implement quantitative decision tools, with algorithmic experiments.

courses.name: Networks & Operating Systems
courses.contribution: Direct: network protocols and operating-system resources, scheduling and memory management provide technical digital-infrastructure content.

courses.name: Database Management Systems
courses.contribution: Direct: relational design, normalisation, SQL and query processing provide the data-management layer of digital systems.

courses.name: Software Development
courses.contribution: Direct: software design, programming paradigms, testing and version control turn computational methods into implemented digital systems.

courses.name: Algorithms & Data Structures
courses.contribution: Direct: algorithm design, data structures and complexity analysis supply efficient computational methods for the data-systems programme.

courses.name: Introduction to Data Science
courses.contribution: Direct: cleaning, manipulating and visualising data and a data-analysis project support empirical system and policy investigation; no policy-specific project is promised.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.contribution: Direct: regression, classification, dimension reduction, validation and predictor projects develop empirical modelling for data-informed decisions, without guaranteeing policy datasets.

courses.name: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
courses.contribution: Direct: neural-network methods and time/text/image learning extend predictive analysis; no claim of public-sector application or explanatory policy causality.

courses.name: Introduction to Programming
courses.contribution: Direct: structured programming, functions, testing and debugging implement the computational foundation of model-based analysis.

courses.name: Mathematical Methods
courses.contribution: Direct: calculus, differential equations and a Mathematica dynamic-model project establish mathematical model formulation; linear algebra is taught separately.

courses.name: Linear Algebra
courses.contribution: Direct: matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalues and linear systems provide the mathematical structure used in quantitative system analysis.

courses.name: Computational & Numerical Methods
courses.contribution: Direct: numerical roots, quadrature and differential/linear-system solution with error and stability analysis support computational modelling.

courses.name: Linear Systems
courses.contribution: Complementary: continuous/discrete linear dynamics, transforms and feedback give rigorous physical-system modelling for the energy concept. Linear time-invariant analysis is not socio-technical ABM or system dynamics.

courses.name: Probability & Statistics
courses.contribution: Direct: probability, statistical inference, Bayesian ideas and sampling simulation support measurement and decision uncertainty.

courses.name: Governance of Sustainability
courses.contribution: Direct: institutions, power, networks, stakeholder matrices and policy evaluation examine collective sustainability decisions; energy/climate cases and policy advice connect governance with technical change.

courses.name: Sustainability Essentials I
courses.contribution: Direct: integrated physical sustainability, thermochemical/mechanical foundations and simple dynamic models introduce resource and environmental constraints on energy systems.

courses.name: Sustainability Essentials II
courses.contribution: Complementary: waves, chemical principles, material behaviour and engineering/greenwashing cases strengthen the physical and evaluative basis for renewable design, without supplying process engineering.

courses.name: Climate Change
courses.contribution: Direct: climate-system mechanisms and human influence connect energy transition decisions to their physical environmental consequences.

courses.name: Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy
courses.contribution: Direct: environmental, social and cost life-cycle assessment of products, processes and services provides explicit criteria for evaluating transition choices.

courses.name: Energy & Sustainability
courses.contribution: Direct: renewable resources, conversion, storage, grids and demand management, quantitative exercises and mini-grid/Polysun activities supply substantial actual energy-system study.

courses.name: Renewable System Design
courses.contribution: Direct: energy-demand/conservation and solar, wind and bioenergy are examined through technical-economic analysis and a partner report. No thermodynamic-cycle or industrial-process sequence is inferred.

courses.name: Law, Society & Justice
courses.contribution: Direct: public/private law, constitutional/administrative principles and legal interpretation support the institutional analysis of public decisions. It is not the complete Dutch public-administration sequence.

courses.name: Ethics
courses.contribution: Direct: normative theories, moral argument and ethical essays supply critical evaluation of decisions and responsibility; not engineering-safety certification.

courses.name: European Union Politics
courses.contribution: Direct: EU institutions, interests, agenda setting, legislation and implementation are studied through empirical amendment coding and process tracing, giving concrete multi-actor policymaking rather than generic governance context.

courses.name: Public Policy Analysis
courses.contribution: Direct: public-policy formation, globalisation and a sugar-policy case develop policy analysis and policy memos; energy/digital assignments are not guaranteed.

courses.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
courses.contribution: Direct: qualitative research design, interviews, documents, coding, reflexivity and an actual team inquiry support actor- and institution-focused policy research.

advisoryProgression: Foundational mathematics/programming and relevant probability/linear algebra precede dependent modelling/decision work; energy foundations precede design. The two fixed programmes meet formal constraints; no speculative prerequisites.

transportAttempt.concept: Transport/logistics systems analysis and governance, derived from10951/10964 before consulting UCR

contentFindings.DISCOMP312: Actual max-flow/dynamic-programming/network algorithms support quantitative flow analysis but not transport engineering, service operations or logistics applications.
contentFindings.ENSSUST315: GIS/remote sensing for land/environment/disaster/agriculture supports spatial information; no transport-routing or mobility curriculum inferred.
contentFindings.ENSDELT111: Nature-based civil/coastal infrastructure and ecological design; port cases do not constitute logistics operations.
contentFindings.ENSDELT211: Water/delta engineering, governance and justice; not transport systems.
contentFindings.BENENTR312: International business, trade and market entry; not a logistics methods course.
contentFindings.ENSDELT312: Substantial multi-actor sustainability governance, already core; no prescribed transport-policy sequence.

transportAttempt.disposition: not-feasible academically as a transport/logistics programme, irrespective of possible numerical scheduling. The real spatial/water/algorithm content is recognised rather than discounted for missing enrichment. Relabelling it as transport would overstate its defining weight. No alternative water programme is invented from transport evidence.

alignments.rationale: The full actor/objectives/causal/system-diagram and multi-criteria problem-analysis sequence has no separate adequate selected counterpart; later policy and decision courses supply related parts without becoming this introductory integrated module.
Dynamic mathematical model formulation and implementation overlap with modelling principles; the wider model taxonomy, stochastic experiments and validation cycle are not reproduced.
No selected course directly teaches the external complex socio-technical simulation cycle, emergence, queues and agents. Linear Systems is physical LTI analysis and cannot stand in for it.
Public/private law, constitutional-administrative principles and legal reasoning are substantial shared content; Dutch public-administration and EU-law breadth differ.
Microeconomic choice and market analysis are central shared foundations; infrastructure-specific economics is less extensive.
Linear algebra is a major explicitly named part of the external module. Differential equations are distributed elsewhere in UCR; this is not a full module equivalence.

No separate selected course substantially covers multivariable calculus alongside linear algebra. Single-variable Mathematical Methods and the separately aligned Linear Algebra do not supply that combined module.
Programming foundations, control structures and implementation overlap directly; the prescribed language, applications and credit weight differ.
Probability and statistical inference are central shared methods; the level, software and balance of applied data analysis differ.
Linear programming, discrete optimisation and decision algorithms directly overlap; the external preference-aggregation and complete graph-theory sequence are not reproduced.
Energy resources, conversion, electricity/storage and demand-system analysis overlap substantially; industrial-network coverage differs.

Thermal-plant and storage-performance analysis with climate effects has no separate adequate selected counterpart. Renewable design is aligned with advanced performance analysis; the full thermal-plant course remains distinct.
Stakeholder reasoning occurs in sustainability governance and policy study, but no separate selected course supplies the dedicated multi-actor-system analysis module.
Normative ethical reasoning is a substantial shared foundation; engineering risk and safety methods remain a gap.

Public goods, market failures and government intervention supply a directly relevant economic foundation; specialised infrastructure ownership, contracting and regulatory economics are not equivalent.

EU institutions, actor interests, decision rules and implementation directly address institutional public decision-making; Dutch administrative-law remedies and the full network-governance sequence differ.
Qualitative case inquiry, interviews, document work and analysis/reporting directly share the principal research method; policy context and project structure differ.
No selected course teaches the prescribed agent-based and system-dynamics modelling methods. Generic programming, linear dynamics and machine learning do not establish this relationship.
Research questions, design, sampling, statistical analysis and methodological limits share the empirical research function; the external policy-oriented multivariate project is more specific.
No selected course guarantees an ABM/system-dynamics socio-technical simulation project; general software or numerical projects are insufficient.

Regression, classification and dimension reduction are substantial shared multivariable methods. Prediction-focused statistical learning is not the complete external conjoint/Q-method and survey-measurement curriculum.
The heat, mass and momentum transfer sequence, transport equations and fluid-flow calculations lack a direct selected counterpart; the title does not refer to logistics.
No selected course supplies the dedicated thermodynamics, exergy, cycle/process simulation and plant-performance sequence.
No selected course supplies industrial unit operations, reactors/separations, flowsheets and mass-balance analysis of industrial clusters.
Genuine 30-EC approved minor remains open; no UCR course is equated with unspecified choices.

No separate selected course teaches electricity/gas/heat market structures and governance options at this specialist depth. Sustainability governance is aligned with the broader socio-technical-governance module; energy cases do not become a full energy-market-governance course.

Institutions, actor power, governance networks, qualitative stakeholder inquiry and policy evaluation directly address the governing of socio-technical sustainability systems. The case emphasis and prescribed external research design differ.
Technical-economic assessment of energy options is a substantive shared educational function; the external linear-programming and network-performance methods are not reproduced by this course.
Compulsory independent 15-EC bachelor project remains distinct from the scheduled taught courses. The standard optional UCR research element is comparison-only.
